successCriteria.description: The AuditLog entity interface is exported from the audit model file and exposes exactly the fields: id, entityType, entityId, action, oldValues (Record<string,unknown> | null), newValues (Record<string,unknown> | null), performedBy (string | null), performedAt (Date), ipAddress (string | null), userAgent (string | null), createdAt (Date).

The IAuditLogRepository interface declares all five operations: findById(id), findByEntity(entityType, entityId), findByPerformedBy(performedBy, limit?), create(entry), findAll(filters) — each with the correct return type (single AuditLog | null for findById, AuditLog[] for collection queries, AuditLog for create).

The PgAuditLogRepository class implements IAuditLogRepository and extends BaseRepository from src/shared/base-repository.ts; it uses the shared pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts for all queries (no direct DB access outside the repository pattern).

create(entry) persists a new audit_logs row with a server-generated id (randomUUID) and createdAt (now), accepts the caller-supplied performedAt, and returns the persisted AuditLog; it throws a typed error when the insert returns no row or a row failing the type guard.

findByEntity(entityType, entityId) returns all audit_logs rows matching both columns; findByPerformedBy(performedBy, limit?) applies an optional LIMIT clause only when limit is provided; findAll(filters) builds a parameterized WHERE clause from any provided filter fields and returns matching rows — all return an empty array (never null) when no rows match.

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/audit/audit.repository.test.ts mock the shared pool and cover every repository method: success path, not-found/empty result, type-guard rejection of invalid rows, and database error propagation — and the full suite passes under `npx jest`.

constraints: No `any` types — use `unknown` with type guards for row-to-entity mapping (HARNESS.json no-any rule, severity high).

All database access must go through the repository pattern — PgAuditLogRepository must use the shared pool via BaseRepository.query, never inline SQL outside the repository (GP-001, HARNESS.json no-direct-db-outside-repository, severity critical).
AuditLog records are immutable — the repository must expose no update or delete operation (GP-002; reconciled architecture states "No update or delete operations — audit records are immutable").
IDs must be generated via crypto.randomUUID() and timestamps via new Date() at the repository layer, matching the established pattern in sibling repositories (ARCHITECTURE.md as-built notes).
Strict TypeScript must pass (tsc --noEmit) with no implicit any and strict null checks enabled; the module must compile cleanly.
outOfScope: AuditService (IAuditService / AuditService) — deferred to Phase 10; this phase covers only the model, repository interface, and repository implementation.
Database migrations / schema creation for the audit_logs table — this phase assumes the table exists per the reconciled architecture; no migration files are produced here.
HTTP routes, controllers, RBAC guards, and Fastify registration for the audit module — deferred to later phases.

Transaction (PoolClient) support in repository methods — the audit repository's create is a single-row insert; multi-step transactional audit writes are orchestrated by the calling service in later phases, not by this repository.

ambiguities.description: The findAll(filters) interface declares an AuditLogFilters type with optional fields (entityType, entityId, performedBy, action, performedFrom, performedTo). PLAN.md only says "findAll(filters)" without specifying which filter fields are supported. The existing implementation already defines performedFrom/performedTo date-range filters, but the phase intent does not enumerate them.
options: Accept the existing AuditLogFilters shape (entityType, entityId, performedBy, action, performedFrom, performedTo) as the canonical filter contract
Restrict findAll filters to only the fields explicitly named in PLAN.md (entityType, entityId, performedBy, action) and drop date-range filters

ambiguities.description: The create(entry) input type is Omit<AuditLog, 'id' | 'createdAt'>, meaning performedAt is caller-supplied. The reconciled architecture confirms performedAt is "caller-supplied (records when the audited action occurred)" while id and createdAt are server-generated. However, it is ambiguous whether the repository should default performedAt to now() when the caller omits it — the current type makes it required (non-optional Date), so omission is a compile error, but a reviewer might expect a fallback.
options: Keep performedAt as a required field in the create input (caller must always supply it) — matches the current Omit type and reconciled architecture
Make performedAt optional and default to new Date() when omitted

entityInvariants.invariant: An AuditLog record is immutable once created — it can be inserted and read but never updated or deleted; the repository exposes no mutation operations other than create.
id and createdAt are always server-generated at the repository layer (randomUUID and new Date respectively); the caller never supplies them — create accepts Omit<AuditLog, 'id' | 'createdAt'>.

performedAt is caller-supplied and records when the audited action occurred, distinct from createdAt which records when the log row was persisted; the two timestamps are independent and must not be conflated.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the matching AuditLog or null when not found / when the row fails the type guard; database errors propagate as thrown errors (no silent swallow).
Returns an array (empty when no matches, never null); rows failing the type guard are filtered out; database errors propagate as thrown errors.
Returns an array (empty when no matches); applies LIMIT only when the optional limit is provided; database errors propagate as thrown errors.
Persists a row with server-generated id and createdAt, returns the created AuditLog; throws a typed error when the insert returns no row or a row failing the type guard; database errors propagate.
Returns an array (empty when no matches, never null); builds a parameterized WHERE clause from provided filter fields; rows failing the type guard are filtered out; database errors propagate.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: PgAuditLogRepository must extend BaseRepository and route all SQL through its query helper (or the inherited findById/findAll/insert helpers) using the shared pool — matching the pattern established by PgEmployeeRepository and the other sibling repositories.

The repository must follow the established row-mapping pattern: a private AuditLogRow interface with snake_case columns, a rowToAuditLog mapper, an isAuditLogRow type guard using unknown + property checks (no any), and a private BaseRepository subclass instance — matching the structure used by PgEmployeeRepository.

The AuditLog entity fields and the audit_logs table columns must match the reconciled architecture exactly: entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at — with indexes on (entity_type, entity_id), performed_by, performed_at, and action.
The audit module's only cross-module dependency is shared-types; it must not import from employee, leave-request, or any other domain module — matching the dependency map (audit → shared-types only).

integrationPoints.why: PgAuditLogRepository extends BaseRepository and uses its query helper for all database access.
The repository uses the shared PostgreSQL pool (transitively via BaseRepository) for all queries — no separate connection management.

The IAuditLogRepository interface is the contract that the future AuditService (Phase 10) and the leave-request/balance services will depend on to write audit records for state-changing operations (GP-002).
